tasks.short: Conduct original research, write findings and separately submit or present them.

steps.what: Define the research question, method and permissions
Retrieve and verify literature and source references for the research
Conduct the study and interpret the findings
Write the research manuscript and presentation narrative from the findings

loop.input: Research plan, verified references and analysed findings
loop.output: Draft sections with source links and explicit limitations
loop.check: Researcher checks each factual claim and interpretation against the supplied findings
loop.stop: One revision pass; unsupported claims or confidential material return the section to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies headings but cannot express the study-specific narrative

steps.what: Check and revise the findings, citations and publication claims
Format the manuscript and references to the selected publication style
Check the final package and submit findings to the selected publication venue
Check and present the research findings at the professional conference

tasks.design: Use {OTHER}, the reference manager and bibliographic search interface, for verified sources and native citation formatting in {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop expresses supplied findings; original research, claim checking, submission through {PARTNER_PORTAL} and conference delivery remain separate human steps.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source navigation, prose drafting and publication formatting add effort around original research.
tasks.enabler_now: Reference tools and bounded source-linked drafting can reuse verified material.
tasks.still_hard: Research design, interpreting evidence and making a defensible contribution.
tasks.human_edge: Original scholarly judgement and responsibility for the published claim.
tasks.altitude: Direct effort toward research validity rather than repeated prose and citation handling.

evidence.claim: Scopus AI offers topic summaries and foundational papers; this supports discovery, not the validity of a research conclusion.
The digest describes fabricated references as a risk, so every cited work must be verified.
Drafting and formatting labour benefit is an unmeasured E1 scenario.

assumptions: The baseline includes original research, manuscript writing, formatting and actual dissemination; delivery shares average across the publication mix.
The researcher creates the plan in s1, verifies identifiers in s2 and produces analysed findings in s3. These are the only drafting inputs; missing evidence returns to manual work.
The researcher selects publication style and venue while revising in s5; formatting in s6 consumes those fields and the checked manuscript. Missing metadata uses manual formatting.
Try native citation and template features before a drafting loop. Ordinary author saves remain fully retained without self-gates.
unknowns: Research confidentiality and allowed drafting environment
Available publication templates and reference metadata
research_questions: Does a source-linked draft reduce total manuscript effort after factual checking and rejected sections?

already_counted.description: Draft review and full research claim checking

incremental.description: Maintain drafting checks and publication styles

approvals.approved_version: Exact formatted manuscript, attachments, author details and venue checked immediately before submission; any change voids approval.
Exact conference narrative, displayed findings and intended audience checked before presentation; changed claims require a new check.

tasks.short: Evaluate assignments, draft feedback and separately publish examiner-confirmed results.

steps.what: Retrieve students' assignments, papers and the applicable marking rubric
Read the class work and assess evidence of learning
Determine grades using the rubric and resolve ambiguous or exceptional answers
Write rubric feedback explaining strengths and improvements in the students' papers

loop.purpose: Draft feedback from the examiner's own notes
loop.input: Passage-linked notes, rubric and already determined grade
loop.output: Draft feedback retaining the examiner's assessment
loop.check: Teacher verifies each comment and ensures the prose does not change the grade or invent evidence
loop.stop: One revision; unsupported comments are written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: A comment bank does not express the assignment-specific explanation

steps.what: Enter the determined grades and reviewed feedback in the gradebook
Check final student mappings and publish grades and feedback to students

tasks.design: Use native rubric and gradebook views in {LMS}, with a bounded feedback drafting step from teacher notes. Reading and grade decisions remain fully human; entry into the unpublished gradebook and actual release to students are separate actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated feedback phrasing and navigating work-to-grade mappings add effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Instructor-note-based feedback drafting is a documented product capability.
tasks.still_hard: Judging the student's reasoning and explaining a defensible grade.
tasks.human_edge: Accountable educational judgement and understanding the student's work.
tasks.altitude: Keep marking decisions human while reducing repeated feedback wording.

evidence.claim: D2L Brightspace Lumi Feedback drafts rubric and text feedback from instructor notes.
The Michigan study reported agreement and revision outcomes without time data; it does not validate this labour estimate.
The labour scenario retains human grade decisions and is E1.

assumptions: The teacher is the authorised examiner for this task; no model assigns grades.

The LMS supplies submitted work and student identity in s1; the teacher produces passage-linked assessment notes in s2 and grades in s3, with capture time counted. Missing identifiers are resolved manually.
Try native rubric comments first; the drafting loop is used only where individual explanation still requires writing.
No second-system rekey is assumed from the digest's single institutional example. Author saves in s5 remain fully retained without approval.
unknowns: Actual volume of repetitive versus bespoke feedback
research_questions: Does reviewed feedback drafting reduce total marking time without changing grades or weakening explanations?

already_counted.description: Human grade determination and feedback draft review

incremental.description: Maintain rubric prompts and sample feedback quality

approvals.approved_version: Exact student identifiers, grades, feedback and release audience in the final gradebook version; changes require a fresh check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 B100 R83.5 gives16.5 gross minus4 upkeep =12.5 net. Low: notes are too sparse for reliable feedback and the rubric requires bespoke explanations; retrieval9, feedback23, entry9 and55 unchanged leave R96; net0. High: passage-linked notes support shorter edits but exceptions remain; retrieval9, feedback16, entry8 and55 unchanged leave R88; net8 after4 upkeep.

tasks.short: Read current literature, exchange ideas and prepare and deliver professional contributions.

steps.what: Find current literature and relevant professional association materials
Read current literature and judge its implications for the field
Discuss developments and questions with colleagues
Serve on professional association committees and consider their business
Write conference presentation material and professional contribution notes
outputs: checked presentation material and contribution notes

loop.purpose: Draft a professional presentation from selected sources and the teacher's argument
loop.input: Verified sources, selected implications and intended audience
loop.output: Draft presentation sections with source links
loop.check: Teacher checks source meaning, novelty and the exact claims to be presented
loop.stop: One revision pass; unsupported or confidential content is written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: A slide template cannot express the source-specific argument

steps.what: Check and give the presentation at the professional conference
inputs: checked presentation material and contribution notes

tasks.design: Configure topic searches in {OTHER}, the bibliographic search interface, and draft professional presentation material in {DOCS} from selected sources. Reading, colleague exchange, committee participation, writing and conference delivery remain separately timed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Searching recurring topics and turning selected insights into presentation prose take repeated effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Saved source searches and source-linked drafting support preparation without replacing professional engagement.
tasks.still_hard: Judging developments and contributing meaningfully to a professional community.
tasks.human_edge: Independent interpretation and reciprocal exchange with colleagues.
tasks.altitude: Use preparation support to sustain more thoughtful professional participation.

evidence.claim: Scopus AI provides topic summaries and foundational papers; this supports source discovery rather than replacing reading.
Preparation savings from saved searches and reviewed presentation drafting are E1 and unmeasured.

assumptions: This is professional updating and contribution; original study production is separately owned by the research task.

The teacher selects topics and verifies sources in s1, develops implications in s2 and supplies the argument to s5. Capture and checking time remain counted; missing source metadata is resolved manually.
Native saved searches and presentation layouts are used first. No automatic source collection, distribution or committee decision is implied.
Working contribution notes are written in s5 rather than hidden inside conversations. Ordinary author saves remain fully retained and ungated.
unknowns: Actual proportion spent preparing professional contributions
research_questions: Do saved searches and draft sections reduce preparation time after checking every presented claim?

already_counted.description: Full reading, colleague exchange and committee participation

incremental.description: Maintain topic queries and source-linked drafting checks

approvals.approved_version: Exact final presentation claims, examples and intended conference audience checked before delivery; revisions require another check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 B100 R89 gives11 gross minus3 upkeep =8 net. Low: new terminology defeats saved searches and most presentation prose needs rewriting; source19, writing13 plus65 unchanged leave R97; net0. High: stable topics improve retrieval while argument edits remain substantial; source17, writing10 plus65 unchanged leave R92; net5 after3 upkeep. Reading and participation are fully retained.

tasks.short: Prepare checked library-science lecture materials and deliver lectures personally.

steps.what: Set lecture objectives for collection development, archival methods or indexing
Retrieve verified readings, collection examples and existing lecture materials
Prepare the lecture narrative, examples and exercises

loop.purpose: Draft lecture materials from verified sources and learning objectives
loop.input: Objectives, student level and verified readings and examples
loop.output: Draft narrative and exercises with source links
loop.check: Teacher checks accuracy, level, source meaning and whether each exercise teaches the objective
loop.stop: One revision; unsuitable examples or missing source support require manual preparation
loop.why_not_simpler: A slide layout cannot adapt explanations to the specific topic and student level

steps.what: Check and revise the lecture content and teaching sequence
Check and deliver lectures, demonstrations and answers to student questions
Record lecture adjustments and follow-up teaching points

tasks.design: Link the course objectives in {LMS} to verified sources from {OTHER}, the reference manager, and reviewed drafting in {DOCS}. Material preparation, academic checking, actual delivery and post-lecture notes are separate steps.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated source retrieval and first-draft explanations consume preparation time.
tasks.enabler_now: Native teaching templates and bounded source-linked drafting can reuse verified examples.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing appropriate examples and responding to students' actual understanding.
tasks.altitude: Spend preparation capacity on better examples and responsive explanation.

evidence.claim: Source-linked lecture drafting and native teaching templates are plausible E1 capabilities; no supplied case measures lecture preparation savings.

assumptions: The baseline includes material writing and existing post-lecture notes as well as delivery.
The teacher supplies objectives and level in s1, verifies sources in s2 and captures follow-up points in s6. Missing material returns to manual preparation.
Native templates and reusable examples precede the model loop. No automatic LMS publication or distribution is proposed.
Author saves during revision and note entry retain their small effort with no self-approval stage.
unknowns: Source access and allowed drafting environment
research_questions: Does source-linked drafting lower total preparation effort after checking topic accuracy and exercise suitability?

already_counted.description: Draft review and full academic revision

incremental.description: Maintain teaching templates and source-linked drafting checks

approvals.approved_version: Exact final lecture narrative, examples and student audience checked before delivery; changed claims or examples are checked again.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 B100 R83.5 gives16.5 gross minus3 upkeep =13.5 net. Low: examples poorly match the level and draft exercises need rewriting; retrieval14, writing23, notes4 plus55 unchanged leave R96; net1. High: existing source examples fit but substantial narrative adaptation remains; retrieval13, writing17, notes4 plus55 unchanged leave R89; net8 after3 upkeep. Delivery and academic revision remain full.
